item.title: Configure SAT bootprep CFS Layers
item.description: Configure SAT bootprep CFS Layers Before running any IUF stages that use sat bootprep, you must add the csm-security layer to your bootprep input file. (ncn-m001#) Locate your management node bootprep configuration. If a previous CSM install or upgrade has been performed, the bootprep file is typically already in your admin directory (e.g., /etc/cray/upgrade/csm/admin/). This may be a site-customized version of the default recipe bootprep, or a completely custom file. Identify whichever bootprep file is actively used for your management node CFS configurations.

item.title: Prepare Images
item.description: Prepare Images Prepare the new images only after product delivery and CFS configuration have succeeded. This stage rebuilds NCN images (master, worker, storage) using sat bootprep. The images are built using the CFS configurations created during update-cfs-config, which include the csm-security layer with security patches. Note: Building new management node images will take about an hour. (ncn-m001#) Run the prepare-images stage. iuf -a ${ACTIVITY_NAME} -m ${MEDIA_DIR} run \ -bm ${BOOTPREP_FILE} -sv ${SITE_VARS} -rv ${RECIPE_VARS} \ -r prepare-images After prepare-images completes, identify the image IDs and CFS configurations it created.

item.title: Deploying Rapid Release Update with IUF
item.description: Deploying Rapid Release Update with IUF This procedure describes how to deploy a Rapid Release Update(RRU) to an operational CSM system using the Install and Upgrade Framework (IUF). It updates the operational CSM release with the CVE patches from csm-security product. The kernels of all the NCNs are updated using CFS to create new NCN images. NCNs are rebooted with the new image to complete the deployment. This procedure is limited to the deployment of the new images to management nodes (NCNs) only.

item.title: Management Nodes Rollout
item.description: Management Nodes Rollout This section updates the kernel running on management NCNs. Storage Nodes Worker Nodes Master Nodes References Next Steps Important: csm-security includes kernel updates, this requires all node types to be rebooted into a new image. The standard docs-csm non-CSM-upgrade workflow (section 2.2) cannot be used here, because it only applies CFS configuration to master and storage nodes without rebooting them. To ensure that all management nodes are rebuilt to include these new csm-security fixes, follow the full image rollout procedures below for all management node types.

item.title: Post-Rollout Verification
item.description: Post-Rollout Verification Post-Rollout Verification Steps Stop the typescript References Next Steps 1. Post-Rollout Verification Steps After all nodes are rolled out, validate the system: Online: Validate CSM Health On-system: /usr/share/doc/csm/operations/validate_csm_health.md Confirm all management nodes are running the expected kernel: pdsh -w $(echo $(ceph orch host ls | grep ncn | cut -f1 -d" " | xargs) $(kubectl get nodes | grep ncn | cut -f1 -d" " | xargs) | sed 's/ /,/g') 'uname -r' |dshbak -c Example output:

item.title: Preparation steps
item.description: Preparation steps Start typescript Ensure latest documentation installed Health validation Prepare for the install Upload Product Media Check and clean old images on storage nodes Next Steps 1. Start typescript (ncn-m001#) If a typescript session is already running in the shell, then first stop it with the exit command. (ncn-m001#) Start a typescript. script -af /root/rru.$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).prepare_for_upgrade.txt export PS1='\u@\H \D{%Y-%m-%d} \t \w # ' If additional shells are opened during this procedure, then record those with typescripts as well.

item.title: Product Delivery and Update CFS Configuration
item.description: Product Delivery and Update CFS Configuration Execute the IUF process-media through deliver-product stages Update CFS Configuration Next steps 1. Execute the IUF process-media through deliver-product stages This stage extracts the tarball, validates the product manifest, uploads RPMs to Nexus, pushes CFS content to Gitea, and registers the product in the product catalog. (ncn-m001#) Run from process-media through deliver-product. Note: For csm-security, there are no required manual actions between pre-install-check and deliver-product, so these stages can be run in a single command.
